additions.reason: The Rebbe's central bechina: 'עִקָּר הַגְּבוּרָה הוּא בַּלֵּב' — the essence of bravery IS the heart (its strength). גְּבוּרָה and חֹזֶק לֵב are the same reality described from two angles. This is the dominant concept of Package 1 and should be the anchor node, with bechina edges to חוזק לב and גיבור.

Explicitly identified as the essence of גְּבוּרָה: 'עִקָּר הַגְּבוּרָה הוּא בַּלֵּב, דְּהַיְנוּ מִי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ חָזָק'. 'מִי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ חָזָק' (one whose heart is strong) is the definition of the גִּבּוֹר. Should have a bechina edge to גבורה.
additions.source_quote: עִקָּר הַגְּבוּרָה הוּא בַּלֵּב, דְּהַיְנוּ מִי שֶׁלִּבּוֹ חָזָק

additions.reason: The Rebbe opens by defining the גִּבּוֹר as 'אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם פַּחַד' — one who has no fear. This is not a causal statement but a defining bechina: the hero IS defined by fearlessness rooted in his strong heart. The גִּבּוֹר is the human embodiment of חֹזֶק לֵב / גְּבוּרָה — he is the same essential quality incarnated in a person. Should have a bechina edge to גבורה and חוזק לב.
additions.source_quote: כִּי הַגִּבּוֹר אֵין לוֹ שׁוּם פַּחַד, וְעִקָּר הַגְּבוּרָה הוּא בַּלֵּב

additions.reason: Used in the same clause as חֹזֶק alongside it: 'מִתְגַּבֵּר עַל־יְדֵי חֹזֶק וְאֹמֶץ לִבּוֹ'. The pairing of חֹזֶק and אֹמֶץ as a unified quality indicates they are bechina-identical: courage (אֹמֶץ) and strength (חֹזֶק) of heart are two names for the same inner reality. Should have a bechina edge to חוזק לב.

The opening statement of the Torah: 'עַל־יְדֵי חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב נוֹפְלִים פְּחָדִים עָלָיו'. Weakness of the heart is the root-nature of the domain of fear — its causal relationship to פְּחָדִים is eitza (between packages), but חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב itself is a bechina of רַךְ לֵבָב (soft-heartedness). Should be the anchor node of Package 2 with a bechina edge to רך לבב.
additions.source_quote: עַל־יְדֵי חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב נוֹפְלִים פְּחָדִים עָלָיו

additions.reason: Rashi (cited by the Rebbe) equates 'הַיָּרֵא' (the fearful) with 'רַךְ הַלֵּבָב' (soft-heartedness). The Rebbe then confirms: 'כִּי עַל־יְדֵי רַךְ לֵבָב... הוּא מִתְיָרֵא, כַּנַּ"ל'. The 'כַּנַּ"ל' is the Rebbe's bechina marker — it means this is AS SAID ABOVE (equating rakh-levav with the fearful state already described). רַךְ לֵבָב IS חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב seen from another angle — both name the same weak-hearted nature. Should have a bechina edge to חלישות הלב.
additions.source_quote: אִישׁ הַיָּרֵא וְרַךְ הַלֵּבָב, פֵּרֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י: הַיָּרֵא וְכוּ', כִּי עַל־יְדֵי רַךְ־לֵבָב, עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה הוּא מִתְיָרֵא, כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: Rashi's gloss equates הַיָּרֵא with רַךְ הַלֵּבָב — they are the same person described by the same inner condition. 'הַיָּרֵא' is the human manifestation of the weak-heart domain (just as הַגִּבּוֹר is the human manifestation of Package 1). The Rebbe reads Devarim 20:8 as defining the fearful man entirely by his soft heart. Should have a bechina edge to רך לבב.

The Rebbe uses פְּחָדִים (fears/terrors) and יִרְאָה (fearfulness) as the experienced manifestation of the weak-hearted domain. Note: the relationship 'חֲלִישׁוּת לֵב → פְּחָדִים' is eitza (cause produces effect). However, פַּחַד as a concept is the defining quality of the יָרֵא and is bechina-identical with יִרְאָה. The Rebbe's use of 'כַּנַּ"ל' links הַיָּרֵא, רַךְ לֵבָב, and מִתְיָרֵא as the same condition. פַּחַד belongs in Package 2 as a bechina of the fearful-weak-heart domain, not as a separate eitza output. Should have a bechina edge to הירא or רך לבב.
additions.source_quote: עַל־יְדֵי חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב נוֹפְלִים פְּחָדִים עָלָיו... וְכֵן לְהֵפֶךְ, רַכֵּי־לֵבָב הֵם מִתְפַּחֲדִים

analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror: This Torah has a clean two-package good/evil mirror: Package 1 (גְּבוּרָה וְחֹזֶק הַלֵּב) is the positive domain of inner heroism; Package 2 (חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב וְהַיִּרְאָה) is its negative mirror. The Rebbe explicitly uses the phrase 'וְכֵן לְהֵפֶךְ' (and conversely / and its opposite) to mark the transition from the good package to the evil one — a rare explicit structural marker. The eitza chain runs from Package 2 to itself (weakness causes fear) and from Package 1 to Package 2's absence (strength eliminates fear).
analysis_notes.causal_note: The statement 'עַל־יְדֵי חֲלִישׁוּת הַלֵּב נוֹפְלִים פְּחָדִים עָלָיו' uses 'עַל־יְדֵי' (through/by means of), which is classic eitza language — weakness of heart PRODUCES fears falling upon the person. This is a causal relationship between the root-nature (חֲלִישׁוּת) and the experienced state (פְּחָדִים). However, within Package 2, the concepts חֲלִישׁוּת, רַךְ לֵבָב, הַיָּרֵא, and פַּחַד are bechina-equivalent names for the same inner reality, not a cause-effect chain between themselves.
